assessments.reasoning: The dated and approved SDC field note names Jules I. Schwartz and repeats its report number in page headers. The title has an open-publication restriction, and its introduction identifies the same-date interpreter scope. The fresh PDF hash and every associated raw page, image and content object range match. The cited physical pages were rerendered and inspected at 139 dpi. The displayed passage at FN-LO-34-2, §2 Variable Definition, opening three paragraphs, printed p. 6 / PDF p. 6 addresses the proposition. The opening §2 paragraphs require every used variable to have its characteristics described by either the program or the Communication Pool. The local mechanism is a variable declaration statement for items or tables. The assessment stays within the named dated SDC document and its scope. It assesses documentary wording, not execution on a specific implementation. The Pool is an express alternative to a description in the program. The text also describes temporary local overrides when central changes are pending. That context supports the claim's two sources of description without making a blanket precedence or layout assertion.

challenge.method: Trace the first three paragraphs and nearby local item syntax. Challenge whether explicitly described means local-only, whether local declarations serve two purposes, and whether the chapter resolves all precedence and layout cases.
challenge.results: The Pool is an express alternative to a description in the program. The text also describes temporary local overrides when central changes are pending. That context supports the claim's two sources of description without making a blanket precedence or layout assertion.

limitations: This claim concerns the February 1, 1960 field note and its described profile.
This concerns the source of a variable’s description. Declaration order, precedence rules, layout and later COMPOOL interfaces require their own evidence.
The February 1960 text says it reflects the same-dated interpreter's capabilities. This review is of the text and does not generalize its declaration rules to later COMPOOL interfaces.
